grading_notes: Accept any sound, behavior-preserving consolidation that satisfies the criterion's spirit, including designs different from the canonical solution (e.g. separate deliberately-distinct transfer owner, variant inputs of any naming/shape, per-resource exception selection tables). No exact method names, signatures, or identifiers from any private reference solution are required to earn credit.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair, exactly one shared policy component interprets HTTP error statuses for the API-requesting operations of both client implementations, and no request-performing operation raises its own status-mapped exceptions from local status conditionals.
rubrics.rationale: This case scatters one library-wide status-to-exception policy across 28 request-performing operations in two client classes; re-centralizing that policy is the defining outcome of the task.

rubrics.criterion: Missing-glossary outcomes are selected per resource family through the shared policy: glossary operations of both API generations raise the glossary-specific not-found exception, while non-glossary lookups keep the generic not-found exception.
rubrics.rationale: The glossary distinction was the first special case pushed out of the shared owner; a repair must re-express it as a policy input rather than as per-operation copies, for both glossary API generations present in this repository.

rubrics.criterion: The translated-document download obtains its retryable document-not-ready outcome for the not-yet-available case through a variant of the shared policy instead of a local branch, while generic service-unavailability handling for other operations is unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The not-ready mapping is the second special case that the injection moved into an endpoint; it is the semantic core of the old mode flag and must become expressible centrally again.

rubrics.criterion: Both pre-signed storage-transfer operations obtain their deliberately plain outcome policy (endpoints without DeepL authorization semantics, any non-2xx fails with an action-specific message, never recommends a retry, carries the status code) through a shared decision point rather than complete per-method copies.
rubrics.rationale: The two transfers in this case are the endpoint-owned policy taken to its conclusion: the shared transfer helper was deleted. Consolidation here means the transfer policy is implemented once, even though its semantics deliberately differ from the API policy.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not merely relocate the duplication — per-method helper extraction, copied blocks moved or reordered, or special-case outcomes deleted outright all leave the failure mode and do not earn credit.
rubrics.rationale: A mechanical sweep or fragment reshuffle already demonstrably quiets a structural check for this repository while breaking the error contract, so only genuine re-ownership counts.

rubrics.criterion: Every operation that owned a local status decision — including the ones whose fragments used unusual shapes (membership tests, inverted delegate-first conditions, literal-status comparisons, loop-built message suffixes) — now delegates through the shared policy with the appropriate variant, and no former fragment site is left behind in either client module.
rubrics.rationale: The injected fragments were deliberately non-templated; a sound repair must find all of them regardless of shape and route them through the policy, not only the easy uniform ones.

rubrics.criterion: The shared fallback's generic behavior for all statuses nobody specializes — including message wording for authorization, quota, generic not-found, bad request, rate limiting, service unavailability, and the unexpected-status text — is unchanged, while the per-operation variants are again expressible through it.
rubrics.rationale: Restoring variant expressiveness in the shared owner is the enabling associated change of this consolidation; its generic outcomes were never part of the scattering and must survive the repair intact.

rubrics.criterion: The consolidation does not absorb unrelated responsibilities: transport retry/backoff timing, response payload parsing and model construction, and pre-request input validation remain outside the policy owner, and previously clean areas of the two client modules are untouched.
rubrics.rationale: This case deliberately excludes status-consuming transport logic and payload interpretation from the relation; sweeping them in would be unrelated churn, not repair.

rubrics.criterion: No residue of the duplicated fragments survives in either client module: the per-operation message-suffix assembly locals and strings, orphaned detail builders, and imports (exception constructors, the status enum) that existed only to support the local fragments are gone.
rubrics.rationale: Each injected fragment carried its own suffix assembly and naming; a complete repair removes that scaffolding instead of leaving dead locals and unused imports behind.

rubrics.criterion: The public surface is exactly as before the refactor: module exports, the class set, public method signatures, and return behavior are unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The scattering was internal policy duplication only; any visible API or export change is collateral damage of the repair, not part of it.

rubrics.criterion: For every operation and every error status, the raised exception type, the exact message text (including the server-message and server-detail suffixes appended exactly when the response JSON carries those keys), the retry recommendation, and the carried numeric status code are identical to before the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The library's error contract is its public behavior; the consolidation in this case must be behavior-preserving to the byte, since downstream consumers branch on types, message text, and retry hints.

rubrics.criterion: The test-asserted outcomes still hold: the glossary-specific not-found exception for missing glossary ids in both generations, the authorization failure on usage and language queries, the rate-limit exception on the hot translation and write-back paths, the quota-exceeded exception on usage, and the generic not-found message when polling a document.
rubrics.rationale: These are the observable anchors of the same policy that the case scatters; losing any of them is a direct regression of the case's behavioral boundary.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not silently weaken outcomes the public suite never exercises: the document download's not-ready mapping, the plain fail-never-retry behavior of both pre-signed storage transfers, the delegation of the two inverted delete forms, and every retry recommendation remain exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: Several injected sites have no direct test coverage in this repository (the not-ready mapping and the transfer policies), so passing tests alone is insufficient; this rubric is the specific guard against the cheapest false repairs for those paths.

rubrics.criterion: The repository's full existing test suite passes without modification after the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The whole suite was green both before injection and after it; it is the hard behavioral gate for this case and any repair that does not keep it green regresses the library.
